chunks: "The diyah of the Jew and the Christian is four thousand dirhams, and the diyah of the Magian is eight hundred dirhams." And he also said: "Indeed, the Magians have a book called Jāmās."

Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan said: The proper way regarding these reports is that we interpret them as applying to one who habitually kills the People of dhimmah. For whoever is like that, the Imam may impose upon him, at times, the full diyah of a Muslim, and at times four thousand dirhams, according to what he deems more beneficial in the situation and more deterrent, so that others may refrain from killing them.
As for one from whom that occurs only rarely, no more than eight hundred is binding upon him, according to what we mentioned first. And that which indicates what we have said is what he narrated:
And what Muḥammad ibn Khālid narrated from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī, from Abī Baṣīr, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: protected non-Muslim subjects under Islamic covenant
key_terms.النَّصْرَانِيِّ: a Christian, mentioned here in the context of diyah
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the legitimate authority who may impose the ruling
key_terms.الْمَجُوسِيِّ: a Magian/Zoroastrian, mentioned here in the context of diyah
key_terms.الْيَهُودِيِّ: a Jew, mentioned here in the context of diyah
key_terms.دِرْهَمٍ: a unit of silver currency used to quantify diyah
key_terms.دِيَةُ: blood money or legal compensation due for unlawful killing

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the diyah of Jews, Christians, and Magians in Shia hadith literature?
ai.summary: This passage discusses rulings concerning the diyah for non-Muslims under protection, especially Jews, Christians, and Magians. It also presents Shaykh al-Ṭūsī’s reconciliation of the reports by distinguishing between a habitual killer, for whom the Imam may impose a stronger penalty, and one for whom such killing is an isolated occurrence.
